author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores the power professionals have to prevent a toxic boss from stripping away their identity at work. It also highlights the importance of maintaining balance—prioritizing personal life and being fully present, even when a toxic workplace pressures you to put your job first. 

Natalie Parker is the founder of Natalie Parker Enterprises, a consulting, coaching, and media brand helping organizations and individuals navigate workplace culture, accountability, and leadership challenges. Through her podcast So Your Boss Sucks, Now What?, she empowers employees to endure, excel, or escape toxic leadership while helping executives build healthier, more accountable organizations. With expertise spanning HR, learning and development, and organizational transformation, Natalie blends storytelling, research, and practical strategies to spark courageous conversations. Her mission is to cultivate bold leaders, thriving teams, and workplaces where accountability drives both purpose an
title: How to handle a bad boss | Natalie Parker | TEDxParrish Street

author: TEDx Talks
description: 500 billion cups are thrown away every year. Just cups. The majority of them made from petroleum, used for five minutes, and discarded forever. We cannot recycle our way out of a problem of that scale, because even recycling is a single-use solution. Durable reuse infrastructure means buidling a network of standardized, returnable packaging systems that treat every container as an asset rather than waste. Reuse systems already exist in Colombia, Indonesia, the Netherlands, France, and beyond. Now, a remarkable coalition, from concert venues and multinationals to NGOs and governments, is actively building the standards and financing tools to scale these systems globally. Amy Larkin is a circular economy strategist and co-founder of PR3: Global Alliance to Advance Reuse, an organization that has assembled over 80 leaders to set the standards for a new global reuse industry. She has spent decades working at the intersection of business, environment, and systems change, and is a champion
title: Recycling is not the answer. Reuse is. | Amy Larkin | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: Aviation accounts for more than 4% of global emissions. This is set to triple by 2050, yet planes cannot run on batteries. In a race to electrify the economy, liquid fuel is required in hard-to-solve pieces of the climate puzzle. One answer could be bamboo. The fast-growing plant can be converted into sustainable aviation fuel through a clean biorefinery process requiring no engine modifications. Meanwhile, bamboo cultivation can restore degraded land and create jobs in some of the world's poorest regions without competing for farmland. It is no longer a question of whether we can replace fossil fuels, but rather: are we willing to pay the true environmental costs of the fuels we rely on today? Camille Rebelo is an entrepreneur and clean technology pioneer who has spent 14 years building a blueprint for bamboo-based bioeconomies across three continents and five countries. Her work has restored more than 100,000 acres of degraded land, created over 2,500 jobs, and produced a replicable
title: Why electrification alone will not get us to net-zero | Camille Rebelo | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: Every year, billions of pounds of plastic packaging are used once and thrown away. Most of it ends up in the ocean. What if wherein lies the problem also lies the solution? Researchers are unlocking seaweed's potential as a scalable, sustainable packaging material by solving a key engineering barrier that has prevented wide adoption. A "generous material", seaweed grows without fresh water, fertilizer, or soil, and returns nutrients to the system after use. It is already farmed on every continent except Antarctica, and a sustainable expansion of the seaweed sector could create 100 million jobs worldwide. The next wave of regenerative materials is already here.  Julia Marsh is the co-founder and CEO of Sway, a materials company building the next generation of packaging from seaweed. She started Sway after years of watching the plastic crisis worsen with no scalable alternative on the horizon, and set out to prove that nature had already solved the problem. Sway's seaweed-based films an
title: Turning the tide on single-use plastics | Julia Marsh | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if governments were designed not for control, but for discovery? Drawing from experiments in Singapore, Li Hongyi shows how small, empowered teams and citizen participation can expand a government’s ability to solve problems. It offers a new model for public innovation at scale. What if the future of government is built from the ground up? Li Hongyi is the Director of Open Government Products, a team transforming how technology serves the public good in Singapore. He leads efforts to build digital tools that make everyday life simpler, smarter, and more connected for citizens. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Imagining Government from the Ground Up | Li Hongyi | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: From seashell-inspired ceramics to fungus-grown composites, a new class of materials is emerging. Hortense Le Ferrand explores how bio-inspired design can create high-performance, biodegradable alternatives for everything from electronics to buildings. The future of materials may not be manufactured, but grown. Dr. Hortense Le Ferrand is an Associate Professor at Nanyang Technological University who leads pioneering research in sustainable materials inspired by nature. Her work bridges engineering and nature-inspired design, imagining a future where we can create and grow materials as elegantly and efficiently as the natural world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What if We Could Grow Our Materials? | Hortense Le Ferrand | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: Caregiving is often invisible and hard to put into words. Alecia Neo explores how movement can help express the emotional complexity of care, offering new ways to understand ourselves and others. Through shared gestures, care becomes something we can see, feel and learn from. When care becomes visible, it can be felt, shared and learned. Alecia is an artist whose work explores care, connection, and community through participatory art and movement. She creates platforms that invite others to reflect on what it means to give and receive care, reimagining empathy as a shared, creative act. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What if Care Could Be Choreographed? | Alecia Neo | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: There is often a hidden gap between losing someone and saying farewell. Angjolie Mei explores how this space can be reclaimed, allowing families to connect, express love and find closure. Even in grief, there can be gentleness and choice. Angjolie Mei is the founder of The Life Celebrant, a leading funeral company in Singapore that redefines how farewells are experienced. A second-generation funeral director, she has spent over two decades transforming the industry through compassion, innovation, and a belief that every goodbye deserves dignity and meaning. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What Happens Between Death and Goodbye | Angjolie Mei | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if failure wasn’t something to avoid, but something to embrace? In Singapore, where getting things right often matters, failure can feel uncomfortable. Drawing from the world of clowning, Shanice shows how learning to “flop” can transform our relationship with fear, creativity and resilience. Sometimes, play is what helps us move forward. Shanice Stanislaus is a performer and theatrical clown who uses humour and play to explore vulnerability and courage. Through her work, she invites audiences to rediscover the joy of imperfection and the freedom that comes with embracing our playful, human selves. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Your Clown Is Here | Shanice Stanislaus | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: We often treat tradition as something to preserve, but not to change. Through the guzheng, Mohamed Faizal shows how reinterpreting a traditional instrument across cultures can create new meaning, connection and identity. When we work within limits, creativity finds new paths for tradition to stay alive. Mohamed Faizal is a Malay guzheng artist dedicated to bridging cultures through music. Trained in a traditionally Chinese instrument, he brings a fresh perspective by blending classical techniques with influences from Malay, Middle Eastern, and contemporary music. Through his performances and collaborations, Faizal showcases how cultural exchange can create new forms of harmony, using sound as a bridge between traditions, identities, and generations. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What a 21-String Instrument Teaches About Creativity | Mohamed Faizal | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: Reintegration isn’t just about systems, it’s about people. From Singapore, Andrew Ong shares how a cycling community brings together individuals from all walks of life to support ex-offenders in rebuilding their lives. Sometimes, a new circle is all it takes to change a future. Andrew is the co-founder of Break the Cycle, a ground-up initiative that empowers ex-offenders to rebuild their lives through cycling, mentorship, and community. Drawing from his own journey, he advocates for second chances and the power of belief to restore dignity and hope. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why Second Chances Need Community | Andrew Ong | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description: We often look to technology to solve environmental crises, but what if the answer is simpler? Singaporean Leon Boey shares how community-driven reef restoration can rebuild marine ecosystems at scale. In the face of climate loss, he offers a radically accessible path to regeneration. Leon Boey, a diver turned ocean restorer, has spent over 15 years rebuilding coral reefs across Southeast Asia. He leads Livingseas Foundation, a large-scale coral restoration initiative in Bali, that combines practical reef restoration with eco-tourism and education. Through partnerships with local communities, divers, and scientists, Leon is proving that reef recovery is not a distant dream but a living, growing reality beneath the waves. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why Technology Alone Won’t Save Our Reefs | Leon Boey | TEDxSingapore

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Plongeons dans l’intimité et les méandres de l’imaginaire de Ben Aymerich, magicien et mentaliste. Entre illusions visuelles et expériences personnelles, il dévoile comment notre cerveau peut nous tromper… et aussi nous aider à avancer.
En révélant les coulisses de son parcours et de son évolution, Ben nous invite à regarder autrement ce que nous croyons impossible et à retrouver l’humanité parfois dissimulée derrière nos rôles et nos illusions. Magicien professionnel et mentaliste depuis près de quinze ans. Véritable « couteau suisse » de l’illusion, il crée des expériences sur mesure, capables de surprendre, d’émouvoir et de marquer durablement les esprits. Avec un angle original et unique, il mêle magie, psychologie et narration pour interroger nos perceptions, révéler l’invisible et inviter au questionnement intérieur. Ses interventions ne sont pas de simples numéros : elles sont des ponts entre le réel et l’imaginaire, des invitations à s’émerveiller autrement. Ben croit que l’il
title: Être humain dans un monde fait d'illusions | Ben Aymerich | TEDxIAEMontpellier

author: TEDx Talks
description:
EN: 
Drawing from her journey as an Olympic sailor, this talk explores the role of fear, pressure and vulnerability in high-performance environments. From the obsession with control to the power of trust and shared responsibility, it shows how accepting one's emotions can transform both performance and identity. Ultimately, it reframes vulnerability not as weakness, but as a form of courage.
IT: 
Partendo dalla sua esperienza come atleta olimpica, questo talk esplora il ruolo della paura, della pressione e della vulnerabilità nei contesti ad alta performance. Dal bisogno di controllo alla scoperta della fiducia e della condivisione, mostra come accettare le proprie emozioni possa trasformare sia la performance che l'identità. In definitiva, la vulnerabilità non è debolezza, ma una forma di coraggio. Pluripremiata velista olimpionica, allenatrice e dirigente sportiva. Ha rappresentato l’Italia in quattro edizioni dei Giochi Olimpici, ed è stata la prima donna a guidare un equipaggio fe
title: L' angolo di incidenza | Giulia Conti | TEDxSalò

author: TEDx Talks
description: Nguyen Bao Han from class ADP-9A at PennSchool takes the stage with a powerful message about navigating truth in the digital age. In “Learning to Think Critically in the Digital Age: Can We Trust Everything Online?”, Bao Han explores how quickly fake news can spread and how easily people can be misled in today’s fast-paced online world. Through her engaging talk, she challenges the audience to become more thoughtful digital readers by checking reliable sources, recognizing hidden bias, and taking a moment to pause before reacting or sharing information. Bao Han reminds us that in a world overflowing with information, critical thinking is one of the most important skills we can develop. Her message encourages students to slow down, question what they see, and make wiser decisions online. A student at PennSchool This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Learning to Think Critically in the Digital Age | BAO HAN NGUYEN | TEDxYouth@PennSchool

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Nella scienza, come nella vita, se non lo misuri non lo puoi migliorare. Francesca Amorini ci porta dentro il metodo scientifico per ribaltare la nostra percezione del  fallimento, concepito non come obiettivo mancato ma come risorsa. Un intervento che unisce rigore e visione, mostrando come l'analisi critica e la valutazione consapevole degli errori sperimentali siano gli unici strumenti affidabili per navigare la complessità senza perdersi nelle opinioni.
Francesca Amorini, laureata in Fisica Nucleare Sperimentale all’Università di Catania, dove ha conseguito anche il dottorato di ricerca, ha svolto per anni attività di ricerca presso i più prestigiosi istituti quali, tra gli altri, l’INFN (Italia) , l’IPN di Orsay (Francia), il CERN, il MSU (Stati Uniti) , GANIL (Francia). E’ stata portaparola di numerosi esperimenti di Fisica Nucleare Presso i Laboratori Nazionali del Sud, ideatrice di rivelatori di particelle innovativi, relatrice presso numerose conferenze internazionali.Vincitr
title: Oltre il risultato: perché i dati e gli errori raccontano la verità | Francesca Amorini | TEDxGiarre

author: TEDx Talks
description:
E se l'aula scolastica, così come la conosciamo, fosse ormai obsoleta? In un'era dominata dall'AI, il modello educativo standardizzato mostra tutte le sue crepe. Erika Di Martino, pioniera dell'homeschooling in Italia, ci invita a una provocazione radicale: smettere di educare all'uniformità e iniziare a educare alla libertà. Scoprite come trasformare l'apprendimento da obbligo istituzionale a scelta sartoriale, preparando le nuove generazioni a un futuro dove la curiosità sarà l'unica vera competenza.
Ricercatrice e divulgatrice nel campo dell’educazione, presidente della Fondazione Libera Schola, ente impegnato nello studio e nello sviluppo di modelli educativi flessibili e rispettosi della pluralità delle persone. È madre di cinque figli che non hanno mai frequentato la scuola tradizionale, un’esperienza che ha contribuito a orientare il suo lavoro di osservazione e ricerca sul campo.
Da anni lavora con famiglie, studenti e professionisti in Italia e all’estero, analizzando cosa ac
title: E se l'aula non servisse più? Educare alla libertà nell'era dell'AI | Erika Di Martino | TEDxGiarre

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the greatest investment in a child isn’t money, but belief? This talk explores the powerful role of the people who support, guide, and invest in us, often without expecting anything in return. It’s a heartfelt reflection on gratitude, opportunity, and why a good education is never achieved alone. Year 12 student at Scarborough College This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Best Thing You Can Buy Your Child is Education | Kendall Burrows | TEDxScarborough College Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Three Minute Thesis: Can a feminist read a Romantic novelist and still remain a feminist? Olive, a final‑year Arts and Humanities student at Carlow College, explores this question through her dissertation, which examines the many different ways feminism can be interpreted and expressed. Olive is a final‑year Arts and Humanities student at Carlow College, where her academic work explores the many pathways through which feminism can be understood and expressed. Her dissertation examines how feminist perspectives can engage with, reinterpret, and challenge Romantic literature, asking what it means to be a feminist reader today. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Can a feminist read romantic novels and remain a feminist  | Olive Townsend | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: Romanticism idealised solitude as the source of poetic truth. Derek offers a different view: poetry thrives through connection. He traces the journey of one poem—from being sparked by another poet’s work, to beginning in an online class, to growing through research, collaboration and even translation into Greek. Dr Derek Coyle is a poet and academic whose work has appeared widely across Ireland, Britain and the United States. A former Poetry Ireland ‘Introductions’ poet and multiple-time finalist for both the Patrick Kavanagh Award and the Bradshaw Prize, he has read his work in venues from Ireland and Scotland to Sweden and the U.S. Derek’s research focuses on Irish and international poetry, especially questions of place and the intersections of poetry, theology and philosophy. His publications include numerous journal poems, essays, and two poetry collections, including Reading John Ashbery at Costa Coffee, Carlow, which was shortlisted for the Shine Strong Award. He holds degrees f
title: No Wandering Lonely: Journeying Toward Poetry with Others' | Dr Derek Coyle | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: 2026 marks 150 years since the birth of Sir Ernest Shackleton, revered Antarctic explorer and history’s most celebrated survival leader, in Kilkea, Co. Kildare. This presentation reframes Shackleton not simply as a heroic polar adventurer, but as a pioneering, intuitive master of psychology whose real achievements lay in reading people, managing morale, and fostering cohesion against near-insurmountable odds. His story is often told as a simple parable of indefatigable will or inspirational leadership, yet closer inspection of his writings reveals not only a keen awareness of psychological complexity, but an urgent diligence in strategically protecting the emotional wellbeing on which his party’s resilience depended. Shackleton’s choices — from the bold abandonment of the Endurance to the careful allocation of tasks, food, companionship, and even humour — demonstrate a leader who understood minds as acutely as he understood the ice. This presentation restores that psychological prowes
title: Shackleton at 150: Polar Psychologist | Dr Dylan Colbert | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: Biodiversity is a practical way of seeing land, shaped by years of watching weather, soil, hedges and water in rural Tipperary. This talk contrasts that grounded knowledge with the modern efficiency driven farming model, showing how the wider system has shaped what counts as success.  Ailbhe Gerrard is a farmer, beekeeper, researcher and agricultural educator, and the founder of Brookfield Farm on the shores of Lough Derg, Co. Tipperary. With postgraduate training in sustainable development and organic farming in the UK, she returned to Ireland to build a regenerative, nature-led farm that combines livestock, bees, woodlands and biodiversity work with public learning and collaboration. Over the past fifteen years she has developed Brookfield as both a working farm and a place of exchange, convening farmers, artists, scientists and communities through the Field Exchange programme to explore practical climate and biodiversity solutions on the ground. This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: Rewriting the Narrative: Biodiversity is an agricultural skill | Ailbhe Gerard | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: Regina explores the power of regenerative tourism, an approach rooted in community-led planning and a return to cultural heritage. She shows how centering local voices, traditions, and shared history can transform tourism into a force that strengthens communities. Regina Dunne is a public historian and heritage specialist from County Laois whose work focuses on local history, women’s history, genealogy and digital engagement with the past. A graduate of Carlow College’s BA (Hons) in English & History and its MA in Irish Regional History, she has built a career connecting communities with their heritage through research, storytelling and public history projects. Regina is the author of Opening a Window on the Past, exploring the lives of pioneering Laois women. Regina is the Tourism Strategy Manager with Dublin City Council, where she leads the implementation of the city’s sustainable tourism strategy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independentl
title: Cultural Heritage: A Catalyst for Regenerative Tourism?  | Regina Dunne | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: Adam explores whether Irish identity carries measurable commercial value by comparing creators who foreground Irishness in their work with those who do not. Using a data‑driven, mixed‑methods approach, he breaks down how this question can be analysed and discusses the practical insights that emerge for creators, audiences and industry alike. Adam Clarke is an English and History graduate of Carlow College and works as a Marketing Manager within the UK Videogame Industry. Adam specializes in Influencer Marketing within the gaming sector and has worked with creators such as MatPat, Super Eyepatch Wolf, and Troy Baker in research and commercial capacities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Can you put a price on Irishness? Question for Irish influencers. | Adam Clarke | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: We often hear that the “hard sciences” are the most objective and rigorous fields — but that belief overlooks how research becomes incomplete when it excludes ethical, cultural, and human perspectives. This talk challenges the dominant narrative by showing why true interdisciplinarity means sharing decision‑making, not just inviting occasional input. Allison Stephens is a Fulbright Scholar at Research Ireland and an interdisciplinary researcher in public policy, informatics, and systems design. Drawing on leadership in governance, business operations, and implementation science, she develops decision‑making frameworks that integrate scientific evidence with real‑world insight to strengthen complex systems in diverse international settings. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What's missing from science? The rest of us | Alison Stephens | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: In Ireland’s senior cycle, an intense focus on exam preparation can unintentionally limit students’ creativity and passion for learning. This talk draws on classroom experience and published data to show how students’ behaviour and the quality of their work shift when they’re given freedom to explore a topic versus when they’re constrained by exam‑driven guidelines.  Patryk Hadrys is a post-primary English and History teacher. Patryk completed his PME in Trinity College Dublin, where he specialised in analysing how English as an Additional Language education is structured in post-primary schools in Ireland. He completed his BA English & History in Carlow College, St. Patrick’s, for which he received the Constance Markievicz 2022 Award. His thesis examined the life of young insurgents in Poland during World War II. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Teaching for Thought: When Survival Replaces Creativity | Patryk Hadrys | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: For decades, scientists have struggled with a central puzzle of consciousness: how brain activity gives rise to the vivid, subjective experience of being “me.” But this challenge may stem less from a natural mystery and more from the old conceptual framework we’ve inherited—one shaped by a 17th‑century split between mind and matter. This talk explores how that divide has shaped modern science’s questions, and how philosophy can help us rethink the assumptions that keep us stuck, not by replacing science, but by revealing the blind spots built into its starting point. Dr Killian McGrath is a philosopher and lecturer whose primary research lies at the intersection of phenomenology and the philosophy of mind. His work also engages political philosophy, metaphysics, and continental philosophy of science, as well as broader questions concerning philosophy’s role in understanding the human condition. He currently teaches at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München and lectures in Political Ph
title: Consciousness: Have We Been Asking the Wrong Question?  | Dr Killian Mc Grath | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk reveals how cultural beliefs, medical advice, and class expectations shaped infant‑feeding decisions long before formula existed. Using nineteenth‑century medical texts, social reports, and advertising, it uncovers how mothers who couldn’t breastfeed were pushed toward hiring wet‑nurses—typically lower‑class women whose labour exposed deep social inequalities. By revisiting these hidden histories, this talk challenges the myth that breastfeeding has ever been simple, universal, or free from social pressures. Dr Judy Bolger is Writing Development Tutor and a lecturer in Academic & Digital Skills and Irish History at Carlow College, St Patrick’s. She also works as an Educational Technologist, supporting staff and students in making the most of digital tools and learning approaches across the College. Judy completed her PhD in History at Trinity College Dublin, where she examined motherhood and institutional life in nineteenth- and early twentieth‑century Ireland. Her earlier M
title: Has Breast Always Been Best? | Dr Judy Bolger | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Young people are often seen as unmotivated, but Donnchadh’s experience, shaped by more than 10,000 career conversations with students, shows the opposite. He meets ambitious, thoughtful teenagers trying to make major decisions under intense pressure and the fear of getting it wrong.
In this talk, he reframes career indecision not as a lack of ambition but as a lack of permission: permission to explore, to change direction and to make choices that can evolve over time. Donnchadh O’Mahony is a guidance counsellor, educator and media contributor best known as the host of the hugely popular Leaving Cert Guidance podcast. A Carlow College graduate, he has worked in education since 2008 and is a regular voice in national media, contributing to outlets such as The Irish Independent, The Irish Times, RTÉ Radio 1, RTÉ 2FM and Today FM. Donnchadh is also the founder of FindMyCollegeCourse.ie, an EdTech platform designed to help students navigate college choices with clarity and confidence. An e
title: Most students don't lack ambition, they lack permission.  | Donnchadh O Mahony | TEDxCarlow College

author: TEDx Talks
description: The talk delved into consciousness as the unchanging essence beyond the physical realm. He shared how consciousness is independent, with the brain acting as a filter, and cited the double-slit experiment to suggest its influence on matter. He concluded that we're consciousness experiencing a physical body, emphasizing shared consciousness as the universe's fundamental essence, leading to unity and happiness.  He is the Dean of Engineering at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Amritapuri Campus and the Director of Center for Flexible Electronics and Advanced Materials. After getting a PhD from UT Austin, he worked at Applied Materials, California, for seven years. His research spans electronic, magnetic, 2D materials, hydrogen storage, and electromagnetic shielding, with 66+ publications. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Beyond You | Dr Balakrishnan Shankar | TEDxAmrita University Amritapuri
